requirements.sourceText: 1. Single-variable Calculus: One of the following sequences: MAT 131 - Calculus I 4 credits; MAT 132 - Calculus II 4 credits; OR MAT 125 - Calculus A 3 credits (or MAT 130 /MAT 125); MAT 126 - Calculus B 3 credits; MAT 127 - Calculus C 3 credits; OR AMS 151 - Applied Calculus I 3 credits; AMS 161 - Applied Calculus II 3 credits. Note: Some or all of this requirement may be fulfilled by an appropriate score on the Mathematics Placement Exam, by AP credit, or by comparable means.

requirements.title: Multivariable Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Differential Equations
requirements.sourceText: 2. Multivariable Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Differential Equations: One course in multivariable calculus: MAT 203 - Calculus III with Applications 4 credits OR MAT 307 - Multivariable Calculus with Linear Algebra 4 credits OR AMS 261 - Applied Calculus III 4 credits. One course in introductory linear algebra: MAT 211 - Introduction to Linear Algebra 3 credits OR AMS 210 - Applied Linear Algebra 3 credits. One course in differential equations: MAT 303 - Calculus IV with Applications 4 credits OR MAT 308 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra 4 credits OR AMS 361 - Applied Calculus IV: Differential Equations 4 credits. Note: Students who take both MAT 307 and MAT 308 do not need to take a separate course in linear algebra, since this material is included in those courses.

notes.text: The catalog describes two special options within the major: the Advanced Track option and the Secondary Teacher Education option. This record models only the regular mathematics major. Advanced Track requirements (its own list of 11 items, a suggested first-two-year sequence, and a prerequisite that Requirement 1 be satisfied before enrolling) are not modeled. The Secondary Teacher Education option is described under the Education and Teacher Certification entry and is not modeled. Students should confirm which option they are following with the Undergraduate Mathematics Office.
Mathematics Honors Program (open to junior and senior majors with at least two upper-division MAT courses at B or higher and a 3.00 GPA; seven MAT courses at a 3.50 GPA plus approval) is not modeled.
Requirement 7 allows six credits of graduate MAT courses in place of undergraduate courses. This is noted on Requirement 7 as a manual check and is not modeled.

Under special circumstances, a student may ask the director of undergraduate studies to allow substitution of an equivalent individual program for some or all requirements. This requires director approval and is not modeled.

Allowed course reuse: MAT 331 and MAE 330 may count toward both Requirement 4 and Requirement 8. Course reuse is enabled for this record because of this explicit exception. Requirements 8 excludes courses used for Requirements 5, 6, and 7.

AP credit: a score of 4 or 5 on the BC exam earns credit for MAT 131 and MAT 132 (8 credits). A score of 4 or 5 on the AB exam earns credit for MAT 131 (4 credits). A score of 3 on either exam earns 3 credits applicable toward graduation but not the major.

Students with prior linear algebra or multivariable calculus should see an advisor in the Undergraduate Mathematics Office. A student with some linear algebra may skip MAT 211 and enroll directly in MAT 310.

Placement: the Mathematics Placement Examination determines starting level. Transfer mathematics courses are evaluated for the entry skill and QPS requirements independently of placement results. Students who place into MAT 123 are subject to the placement-dependent note in Requirement 1a.
Mathematics Learning Center offers tutorial help for 100-level courses, and more advanced students can also get assistance there.
